logicalBugs.explanation: The repository activity RSS feed publishes a release-item URL containing refs/tags/ before the tag name. Opening that generated destination displays a full-page 404 instead of release details.

rootCause.explanation: toReleaseLink appends act.GetBranch(), which for tag creation contains refs/tags, rather than the normalized tag name.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The repository activity RSS feed publishes a release-item URL containing refs/tags/ before the tag name. Opening that generated destination displays a full-page 404 instead of release details.

sourceBugs.name: Repository RSS release-item link retains refs/tags and opens a 404

reproductionPaths.expected: A published-release item's link in the repository activity RSS feed should open that release's details using its tag name without the refs/tags/ prefix.
reproductionPaths.actual: The Distribution Fixture Beta item advertises /eval/harbor-handbook/releases/tag/refs/tags/dist-explore-7263b. Opening that URL displays 404 Not Found instead of the release details at /eval/harbor-handbook/releases/tag/dist-explore-7263b.
reproSteps: Sign in to the feed-enabled Gitea fixture and use a repository with a published release on an ordinary valid tag. The recorded case uses eval/harbor-handbook, release Distribution Fixture Beta, tag dist-explore-7263b.
Open the repository activity RSS feed at /eval/harbor-handbook.rss using the repository header's RSS icon. This is distinct from /eval/harbor-handbook/releases.rss, the separate release-list feed.
Locate the published-release item and inspect its link. The recorded item contains /releases/tag/refs/tags/dist-explore-7263b.
Open that feed-advertised item URL and observe the persistent full-page 404. The recorded run opened the URL extracted from the RSS XML; it did not demonstrate clicking a rendered feed-reader item.

guidance.distinctFromExistingReference: This concerns an individual publication item's /releases/tag/refs/tags/<tag> destination in the repository activity feed. The existing RSS channel reference concerns singular /release versus /releases in the release-list feed's channel link.

logicalBugs.explanation: New Release accepts tag names that later fail Git creation, including a 251–255-character filename component or a parent/child ref namespace conflict. Submit replaces the editor with HTTP 500 and a raw Git/filesystem error instead of keeping a recoverable tag-name error in the form.

rootCause.explanation: The release form accepts Git-ref names and length up to 255, while createTag reports only selected invalid-name errors; valid names exceeding filesystem component limits or conflicting with existing ref directories escape as server failures.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The new-release form permits a 255-character tag name, but submitting a 251–255-character ASCII tag replaces the editor with a filename-too-long server error.

sourceBugs.name: Tag names accepted by the form crash creation with HTTP 500

reproductionPaths.expected: If a tag name is allowed by the form but unsupported by tag creation, show inline validation and retain the entered tag, release title, and notes so the user can correct the name. Publishing or creating a tag must not replace the form with an HTTP 500 page.
reproductionPaths.actual: Publish Release with an exact 255-character ASCII tag and Create Tag Only with a separate exact 251-character ASCII tag both return HTTP 500. The error page reports that Git cannot create refs/tags/<name>.lock because the filename is too long.
reproSteps: Sign in with the fixture account and open the seeded harbor-handbook repository → Releases → New Release. Leave the target branch as main.
Enter qa-boundary- followed by exactly 243 lowercase x characters (255 ASCII characters total). Enter a release title and release notes. Do not shorten the tag.
Click Publish Release. Observe the full-page 500 Internal Server Error with Filename too long instead of inline validation.

Separately verified control: return to New Release, enter qa-tagonly- followed by exactly 240 lowercase x characters (251 ASCII characters total), and click Create Tag Only. Observe the same full-page error.

guidance.scope: Grade the full-page server error on a tag length accepted by the form. Inline rejection of an unsupported length is valid expected behavior; do not require the application to support every 255-character tag. Exact boundaries depend on the fixture filesystem.

matchingGuidance.scope: Grade the full-page server error on a tag length accepted by the form. Inline rejection of an unsupported length is valid expected behavior; do not require the application to support every 255-character tag. Exact boundaries depend on the fixture filesystem.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Creating a tag whose name conflicts with an existing parent or child tag namespace replaces the release editor with a raw Git error page.

sourceBugs.name: Hierarchical tag namespace conflicts replace the release form with HTTP 500

reproductionPaths.expected: Reject a parent/child tag namespace conflict with a clear validation error identifying the conflict, while keeping the form and entered release information available for correction.
reproductionPaths.actual: With qa-mo-ns3/slash-v2 already existing, publishing a release tagged qa-mo-ns3 returns 500 Internal Server Error and a raw cannot lock ref message. With v1.0.0 already existing, Create Tag Only for v1.0.0/qa-mo-patch returns the same full-page error; the editable form is gone.
reproSteps: Sign in with the fixture account and open the seeded harbor-handbook repository → Releases → New Release.
Create a disposable tag qa-mo-ns3/slash-v2 targeting main with Create Tag Only.
Return to New Release. Enter tag qa-mo-ns3 and release title Parent namespace conflict, then click Publish Release. Observe 500 Internal Server Error instead of a recoverable validation message.
Separately, with the seeded tag v1.0.0 present, enter v1.0.0/qa-mo-patch in New Release and click Create Tag Only. Observe the parent-tag namespace conflict also returns a full-page 500.

guidance.scope: A validation error rejecting a conflicting tag is correct. Accept this reference only for a parent/child tag namespace submission causing the full-page server error. Long tag-name filesystem limits are covered by the separate accepted-length reference.

matchingGuidance.scope: A validation error rejecting a conflicting tag is correct. Accept this reference only for a parent/child tag namespace submission causing the full-page server error. Long tag-name filesystem limits are covered by the separate accepted-length reference.

logicalBugs.explanation: Below 439px, New/Edit Release controls stretch to the full field width even when they are checkboxes or toolbar buttons. Pre-Release and tag-message checkboxes overlap their labels, checked/unchecked task boxes in Preview become indistinguishable bars, and the legacy editor toolbar can become a tall single-button column.

rootCause.explanation: The max-width 438px CSS applies width:100% to every .field input/button, including native checkbox controls, preview task-list checkboxes and legacy toolbar buttons.

reproductionPaths.explanation: At 390×844 CSS pixels, the New Release form stretches the Pre-Release checkbox input across its label, placing the native checkbox glyph over the text.

sourceBugs.name: Mobile Pre-Release checkbox overlaps its label on the New Release form

reproductionPaths.expected: The checkbox and Mark as Pre-Release label remain separately visible and legible at the mobile viewport.
reproductionPaths.actual: An independent browser at actual 390×844 CSS pixels, scale 1 and DPR 1 showed the unchecked checkbox over the label. Its input measured about 149 pixels wide instead of 15. At a 520-pixel control viewport the input remained 15 pixels wide and sat separately from the label.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval with write access to a repository and open its Releases > New Release form.
Set the viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels and scroll to the Mark as Pre-Release option.
Inspect the unchecked control. The checkbox glyph overlaps the label text. No release publication is needed.
For comparison, widen the viewport to 520 CSS pixels. The checkbox is separately positioned beside its label.

guidance.deduplication: Distinct from the existing mobile Releases-list Pre-Release status-badge clipping reference; this item concerns the New Release form’s checkbox.

matchingGuidance.deduplication: Distinct from the existing mobile Releases-list Pre-Release status-badge clipping reference; this item concerns the New Release form’s checkbox.

reproductionPaths.expected: At phone width the tag-message checkbox keeps its normal small size beside its label, with the label text readable.
reproductionPaths.actual: At 390px on New Release, the tag-message checkbox measured about 346px wide instead of 15px; its glyph was drawn over the label text. At 439px and wider it rendered normally.

Set the viewport to 390×844.
Look at the “Use the title and content of release as tag message” checkbox and observe its glyph overlapping the label text.

rootCause.explanation: release-list-title is a flex row whose badge has no nonshrinking sizing; constrained mobile/tablet title rows compress the badge text.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A newly published Pre-Release displays a clipped “Pre-Relea” badge in the mobile Releases listing, and the clipping remains after refresh.

Inspect the release’s orange badge in the Releases listing. Observe the text clipped to Pre-Relea.
Wait for the page to settle and refresh. Observe the clipping persists.

logicalBugs.explanation: The Create tag action on a commit produces a valid browsable tag, but the Tags page's New Release action cannot publish a release for it.

rootCause.explanation: CreateNewTag stores the supplied commit SHA in Release.Target, while NewReleasePost requires Target to be an existing branch even when converting an existing tag.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The Create tag action on a commit produces a valid browsable tag, but the Tags page's New Release action cannot publish a release for it.

sourceBugs.name: Tags created from commit Operations cannot be published as releases

reproductionPaths.expected: An existing tag created through the application should be usable to publish a release without requiring a branch change.
reproductionPaths.actual: The release form recognizes 'Existing tag.' but Publish Release returns 'Target branch does not exist.' No target branch selector is available for the existing tag. Reproduced with bash/tag and bash-commit-tag from branch commit 6b749e5869 and bash-main-commit-tag from main commit bfa9c3b716. Publishing the seeded tag and converting a tag created through Create Tag Only both succeed.
reproSteps: Sign in as admin and open an existing commit in admin/harbor-handbook (tested main commit bfa9c3b716a7a5bc72060cba3155d9736206a5d0).
Open Operations, choose Create tag, enter a unique tag name such as bash-main-commit-tag, and click Create tag.
Open the repository Tags page; locate the new tag and click its New Release link.
Enter a release title and click Publish Release.
Observe 'Target branch does not exist.' despite the form showing 'Existing tag.'

logicalBugs.explanation: When branch main and tag main point to different existing commits, publishing a new release with branch main explicitly selected creates its tag at the existing main tag commit.

rootCause.explanation: createTag calls GetCommit(rel.Target) using the bare branch name instead of refs/heads, allowing a same-named tag to take precedence.

reproductionPaths.explanation: When branch main and tag main point to different existing commits, publishing a new release with branch main explicitly selected creates its tag at the existing main tag commit.

sourceBugs.name: Release creation resolves a selected branch as a same-named tag

reproductionPaths.expected: The branch target dropdown must resolve the chosen branch reference. Selecting main creates the new tag at refs/heads/main, even when refs/tags/main points elsewhere.
reproductionPaths.actual: The new release links to side-branch commit 698207d676, matching tag main. The selected main branch still points to 4ff25d14a0; no new source commit was created.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded eval/harbor-handbook repository. Confirm main points to 4ff25d14a0 and docs/release-owners points to its child 698207d676.
Use New Release to create a disposable release with tag name main and target branch docs/release-owners. This creates refs/tags/main at the side-branch commit while leaving refs/heads/main unchanged.
Open New Release again, enter an unused tag name such as qa-main-target-proof and a release title. Explicitly choose main from the branch target dropdown and publish.
Inspect the new release commit link and compare the Code view for branch main. The new release incorrectly points to 698207d676 instead of 4ff25d14a0.

guidance.scope: Credit selecting the wrong existing commit during release creation. The separate negative commits-since-release count is already covered by codex-30m-gitea-6; observing that count alone does not establish this reference. A colliding tag name matters; the release display title does not.

logicalBugs.explanation: Tagging a commit on a branch with more history than the default branch makes the tag details show a negative number of commits to main.

rootCause.explanation: calReleaseNumCommitsBehind subtracts release.NumCommits from the target history count; divergent or longer tag histories can yield negative numbers.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Tagging a commit on a branch with more history than the default branch makes the tag details show a negative number of commits to main.

sourceBugs.name: Tag details display a negative count of commits since release

reproductionPaths.expected: A count of commits since a tag must be nonnegative and account for branch ancestry, or show that the tag is on a different branch.
reproductionPaths.actual: Both bash/tag and bash-commit-tag show '-4 commits to main since this release'. Their tagged commit has seven commits in its history while main has three; the displayed count is negative.
reproSteps: Sign in as admin. Use a repository where a non-default branch has more commits than main (tested admin/harbor-handbook: main has 3 commits, tagged branch commit 6b749e5869 has 7).
Open that branch's commit and use Operations → Create tag to create a unique tag.
Open Tags and click the new tag name to view its details.
Observe '-4 commits to main since this release' on the tag details page.

logicalBugs.explanation: Repeating Operations > Create tag with an existing tag name correctly rejects the duplicate but describes the attempted operation as creating a branch.

rootCause.explanation: The shared NewBranchPost duplicate handling flashes repo.branch.branch_already_exists for CreateTag as well as branch creation.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Repeating Operations > Create tag with an existing tag name correctly rejects the duplicate but describes the attempted operation as creating a branch.

sourceBugs.name: Duplicate-tag creation error describes the attempted operation as branch creation

reproductionPaths.expected: Duplicate-tag feedback identifies the attempted operation as tag creation and explains that the tag already exists.
reproductionPaths.actual: The validation message says: Branch "<tag-name>" cannot be created as a tag with same name already exists in the repository.
reproSteps: Use the English locale and sign in with write access to an initialized, unarchived repository. Use a unique disposable tag name; the original observation used a 390×844 viewport.
Open a commit from the repository’s main branch, choose Operations > Create tag, enter the disposable tag name, and create it.
Return to the same commit, choose Operations > Create tag again, and submit the identical tag name.
Inspect the validation message. It says Branch "<tag-name>" cannot be created as a tag with same name already exists in the repository, despite the attempted operation being tag creation.

reproductionPaths.explanation: At a 390×844 viewport, the tag row clips New Release and leaves Delete Tag outside the visible row; ordinary horizontal scrolling on the row and page does not expose the actions.

reproductionPaths.expected: Authorized tag-row actions remain accessible through the rendered UI at a narrow viewport, whether by responsive layout or ordinary scrolling.

Open the repository Tags page and search for the tag. The recorded path was /eval/harbor-handbook/tags?q=v1.0.0.
Inspect the tag action row: only the beginning of New Release is visible and Delete Tag is offscreen.
Attempt ordinary horizontal scrolling on the row and page. Observe that the actions remain clipped or hidden; no tag deletion or release creation is necessary to inspect the defect.

logicalBugs.explanation: A validation error preserves other release fields but loses successfully uploaded files. Correcting the error and saving produces a release/draft without its attachment.

rootCause.explanation: NewReleasePost re-renders on validation error without reconstructing attachment rows from form.Files, so already uploaded UUIDs are omitted on resubmission.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A validation error preserves other release fields but loses successfully uploaded files. Correcting the error and saving produces a release/draft without its attachment.

sourceBugs.name: Tag validation drops the uploaded release attachment

reproductionPaths.expected: Retain completed uploaded-file associations after a recoverable tag validation error, so correcting only the tag publishes the attachment. If the upload cannot be retained, clearly require re-upload rather than silently publishing without it.
reproductionPaths.actual: After invalid..qa is rejected, the title and notes remain but the completed attachment card disappears without a warning. Correcting only the tag and publishing produces Downloads containing only source archives; validation-asset.txt is absent.
reproSteps: Sign in to eval/harbor-handbook and open Releases → New Release. Enter invalid..qa as the tag and fill a release title and notes.
Upload a small text attachment such as validation-asset.txt and wait for its completed file card.
Click Publish Release. Observe the recoverable tag-validation message, preserved title/notes, and missing uploaded-file card.
Change only the tag to an unused valid name and publish. Expand the release Downloads and confirm the uploaded file is missing.

guidance.scope: Credit the attachment association lost across validation and missing from the corrected published release. This does not claim the underlying temporary file bytes were erased.

matchingGuidance.scope: Credit the attachment association lost across validation and missing from the corrected published release. This does not claim the underlying temporary file bytes were erased.

logicalBugs.explanation: Nested list bullets use different styles in the New Release preview and the published notes for the same Markdown.

rootCause.explanation: The published release wraps notes in render-content markup, while the editor preview uses a different rendering/styling container, so nested lists inherit different marker rules.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Nested list bullets use different styles in the New Release preview and the published notes for the same Markdown.

sourceBugs.name: Published release list bullets differ from Preview

reproductionPaths.expected: The same nested Markdown list should use consistent bullet marker styles in Preview and after publishing the release.

Inline code and strikethrough rendered in both.
reproSteps: Sign in with release-write permission and open New Release in an initialized disposable repository.

Enter a unique unused tag and title. In the release notes enter a Markdown heading, a first-level unordered item Added `widget-v2`, a nested unordered item Improved workflow, and another first-level item Supports ~~legacy widget~~ removal. Use ordinary Markdown indentation for the nested item.
Open Preview. Observe a filled circle for the first-level item and a hollow circle for the nested item.

Publish Release and inspect the same notes in the Releases list. The first-level marker is now a hollow circle and the nested marker is a filled square; text, inline code, strikethrough, and list hierarchy remain present.

logicalBugs.explanation: After a lowercase release exists, Gitea rejects a Git-valid tag name that differs only by case as a duplicate in both Publish Release and Create Tag Only.

rootCause.explanation: IsReleaseExist and GetRelease look up LowerTagName using strings.ToLower, treating distinct case-only Git tag names as one record.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After a lowercase release exists, Gitea rejects a Git-valid tag name that differs only by case as a duplicate in both Publish Release and Create Tag Only.

sourceBugs.name: Case-only uppercase tag rejected as duplicate after lowercase release exists

reproductionPaths.expected: Git tag names are case-sensitive. With a lowercase release already published, an uppercase tag differing only by case should be treated as a distinct tag; Publish Release should create its separate release, and Create Tag Only should create the standalone tag.
reproductionPaths.actual: After publishing lowercase tag case-tag-qa, both Publish Release and Create Tag Only reject uppercase CASE-TAG-QA with “A release with this tag name already exists.” The form still identifies the uppercase name as a new tag, and no uppercase tag or release is created.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture admin and open Releases > New Release for eval/harbor-handbook.
Publish a lowercase release using tag case-tag-qa and a disposable title.

Open New Release again, enter uppercase CASE-TAG-QA, and observe the “New tag” helper. Click Publish Release and observe “A release with this tag name already exists.” Confirm the uppercase release was not created.
Open New Release again, enter CASE-TAG-QA, and click Create Tag Only. Observe the same duplicate-release error and confirm no uppercase Git tag was created.

logicalBugs.explanation: Source archive downloads can contain a different commit from the branch/tag being viewed when its short name is ambiguous. A branch sharing a name with a tag can download the tag’s tree, and a tag named as another commit’s full SHA can download that spelled commit instead of its actual target.

rootCause.explanation: The release archive URL uses an unqualified tag name, and archive resolution accepts object IDs and other refs, so a SHA-shaped tag name resolves the spelled commit.

reproductionPaths.explanation: When a release's tag name is the full 40-character SHA of another commit, the release's Source Code ZIP and TAR.GZ downloads contain the commit that the name spells, not the commit the tag points to.

sourceBugs.name: Source archives use the wrong commit for a tag named as an existing full SHA

reproductionPaths.expected: A release's Source Code downloads contain the commit its tag points to, the same commit the release page and /src/tag/<name> show.
reproductionPaths.actual: Both archives return HTTP 200 but contain the commit whose SHA equals the tag name, so files added in the tagged commit are missing. Tags-page and tag Code-menu archive links behave the same. Ordinary and short-SHA tag names on the same commit download correctly.
reproSteps: Sign in to Gitea with the fixture account and open a repository with at least two commits. Note the full 40-character SHA of an older commit.
Add a file in a new commit on the default branch.
Open Releases → New Release. Enter the older commit's full SHA as the tag name, target the default branch, and publish.
Confirm the release page shows the default-branch commit.
Download the release's Source Code ZIP or TAR.GZ. Observe that its commit comment is the older commit and the new file is missing.
As a control, publish a release with an ordinary tag name on the same target and confirm its archive includes the file.

logicalBugs.explanation: In the standard Markdown toolbar used by wiki pages and release notes, a heading button inserts # markers at the caret instead of making the current line a heading. Selecting text and changing heading levels can stack prefixes such as "# ## ### Heading" rather than replace the existing level.

rootCause.explanation: The shared combomarkdowneditor template uses markdown-toolbar-element md-header directly. Its selection-prefix operation is not adapted to select the whole current line or normalize an existing heading prefix, so both caret insertion and repeated level changes retain incorrect Markdown.

analysis.explanation: The shared Markdown editor toolbar delegates heading prefix insertion to its selection-based toolbar action, which operates at the caret/selection and does not replace the line existing heading prefix.

The shared toolbar uses markdown-toolbar-element md-header directly. Its prefix operation uses the current selection/caret, and the integration does not expand the selection to the whole line, allowing ## to be inserted after existing text.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In the release notes editor, clicking a heading toolbar button (H1–H3) with the text cursor at the end of a line, and nothing selected, inserts the # marker at the cursor instead of at the start of the line, so the line doesn't become a heading. With the line selected, the button works.

sourceBugs.name: Release notes heading button inserts the heading marker at the caret instead of the line start

reproductionPaths.expected: Clicking a heading button with only a cursor on a line turns that line into a heading by adding the marker at the start of the line, as it does when the line is selected.
reproductionPaths.actual: With the cursor at the end of 'QA heading toolbar', clicking H1 produced 'QA heading toolbar# ', which renders as a plain paragraph; the malformed text is kept when the release is saved. Selecting the whole line first and clicking H1 produced '# QA heading toolbar' and a heading.
reproSteps: Open New Release (or edit a release) and type a line of text in the notes.
Leave the cursor at the end of the line without selecting anything, and click the H1 toolbar button.
Check where the # marker was inserted and how Preview renders the line.
Select the whole line and click H1 again to compare.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In the release notes editor, selecting text and clicking H1, then H2, then H3 adds another heading prefix each time instead of changing the level, so the text becomes '# ## ### Heading' and Preview shows a level-one heading containing literal '## ###'.

sourceBugs.name: Changing heading levels with the toolbar stacks Markdown prefixes

reproductionPaths.expected: Clicking a different heading button on an existing heading changes its level, leaving a single prefix such as '### Heading'.
reproductionPaths.actual: After H1, H2 and H3 on the same selected text, Preview showed a level-one heading reading '## ### Heading toolbar'.
reproSteps: Open New Release, type a line of text in the notes and select it.
Click H1, then H2, then H3 without changing the selection.
Open Preview and check the heading.

logicalBugs.explanation: If a release's edit form was opened before someone else saved changes, saving it (even after changing only the title) restores the older notes and pre-release setting without any warning, discarding the newer edits.

rootCause.explanation: EditReleasePost assigns form Title/Content/Prerelease to the loaded release and updates it without an expected version, timestamp or original-content conflict check.

reproductionPaths.explanation: If a release's edit form was opened before someone else saved changes, saving it (even after changing only the title) restores the older notes and pre-release setting without any warning, discarding the newer edits.

sourceBugs.name: Saving a stale release editor silently overwrites newer release notes

reproductionPaths.expected: Saving an out-of-date release edit form warns that the release changed, or keeps the newer notes it didn't touch.
reproductionPaths.actual: After tab B saved new notes, saving tab A's stale form with only a title change left the release with the original notes; the newer notes were lost with no warning.
reproSteps: Create a release with some notes.
Open its edit form in two tabs.
In the second tab, change the notes and click Update Release.
In the first tab, without reloading, change only the title and click Update Release.
Check the release's title and notes.

logicalBugs.explanation: If a tag was created on a non-default branch and a release draft is then created for that existing tag, the saved draft shows the target as main instead of the tag's branch. The draft's Compare also uses main, which can wrongly say the branches are equal.

rootCause.explanation: New release defaults tag_target to the repository default when the tag record has no branch target, then persists the posted target without deriving the tag ancestry/branch.

reproductionPaths.explanation: If a tag was created on a non-default branch and a release draft is then created for that existing tag, the saved draft shows the target as main instead of the tag's branch. The draft's Compare also uses main, which can wrongly say the branches are equal.

sourceBugs.name: A release draft for an existing tag shows main as its target instead of the tag's branch

reproductionPaths.expected: A release draft for an existing tag keeps the tag's real target, both on the edit page and in comparisons.
reproductionPaths.actual: A tag created from docs/release-owners, used for a new release draft, reopened as "<tag> @ main"; publishing it showed "-1 commits to main since this release".
reproSteps: Create a tag from a non-default branch using Create Tag Only.
Start a New Release, type that existing tag name, and save it as a draft.
Reopen the draft and check the target shown next to the tag.

logicalBugs.explanation: In the EasyMDE Markdown editor used for wiki pages and release notes, toolbar tooltips advertise formatting shortcuts such as "Bold (Ctrl-B)", but pressing the shortcut leaves selected text unchanged. Clicking the corresponding Bold or Italic toolbar button works.

rootCause.explanation: switchToEasyMDE replaces CodeMirror extraKeys with a new map containing quick-submit and mention-navigation handlers. This discards EasyMDE formatting key bindings while its toolbar still advertises them. The Ctrl-B tooltip in the release report identifies this EasyMDE path even though that report calls it the enhanced editor; the standard textarea toolbar uses the different "Add bold text" tooltip.

analysis.explanation: The toolbar provides a Bold shortcut tooltip, while the enhanced editor custom key bindings do not install an equivalent bold handler for the textarea mode.

After EasyMDE creates its default keymap, switchToEasyMDE sets extraKeys to a new map containing quick-submit and mention-navigation handlers. It replaces the formatting shortcut bindings while toolbar titles still advertise them.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In the release notes enhanced editor, the Bold button's tooltip says "Bold (Ctrl-B)", but pressing Ctrl+B on selected text does nothing; clicking the Bold button works.

sourceBugs.name: Release notes editor ignores its advertised Ctrl-B bold shortcut

reproductionPaths.expected: Pressing Ctrl+B on selected text makes it bold, as the tooltip says.
reproductionPaths.actual: Pressing Ctrl+B on selected text left it unchanged and Preview showed plain text; clicking the Bold button on the same selection added ** and Preview showed bold.
reproSteps: Open New Release (or Edit Release) and switch the notes to the enhanced editor if needed.
Type some text, select it and press Ctrl+B.
Check the text and Preview, then compare with clicking the Bold button.

logicalBugs.explanation: On a repository's Tags page, after searching, clearing the search box and submitting, pressing the browser's Back button shows the earlier filtered results again but leaves the search box empty, so the page doesn't show what it's filtered by.

rootCause.explanation: The tag search input relies on browser form restoration and has no history-state synchronization from the query URL; cached results can be restored with a later input value.

reproductionPaths.explanation: On a repository's Tags page, after searching, clearing the search box and submitting, pressing the browser's Back button shows the earlier filtered results again but leaves the search box empty, so the page doesn't show what it's filtered by.

sourceBugs.name: Going back after clearing the tag search shows filtered results with an empty search box

reproductionPaths.expected: After going back to a filtered tag list, the search box shows the active query.
reproductionPaths.actual: Back restored the filtered tag results, but the search box showed only the 'Search tags...' placeholder.
reproSteps: On a repository's Tags page, search for a term that filters the list.
Clear the search box (for example with ×) and submit.
Press the browser's Back button and compare the results with the search box.

logicalBugs.explanation: Downloading a release's source code as ZIP (or as a bundle) from the web returns a correct ZIP, but the response's Link rel="immutable" header, which tells download tools the permanent URL for the same file, points to the .tar.gz archive. Following it returns a gzip tarball instead of the ZIP.

rootCause.explanation: The response Link header hardcodes .tar.gz instead of using the requested archive format.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Downloading a release's source code as ZIP (or as a bundle) from the web returns a correct ZIP, but the response's Link rel="immutable" header, which tells download tools the permanent URL for the same file, points to the .tar.gz archive. Following it returns a gzip tarball instead of the ZIP.

sourceBugs.name: ZIP source download advertises a TAR.GZ permanent link

reproductionPaths.expected: The immutable Link header on a ZIP download points to the permanent .zip URL for the same revision, which returns the same ZIP.
reproductionPaths.actual: The ZIP download's Link header pointed to /api/v1/repos/<owner>/<repo>/archive/<sha>.tar.gz?rev=<sha>; requesting it returned a gzip TAR archive with different bytes. The TAR.GZ download's header and the API ZIP download's header were correct.
reproSteps: On a repository's release or branch, download Source Code (ZIP) and inspect the response's Link header (rel="immutable").
Request the URL from that header.
Compare the file format and bytes with the original ZIP download.

logicalBugs.explanation: Draft releases are hidden from users without write access on the web (the release page returns 404 and the draft isn't listed), but a read-only collaborator can fetch the draft's title, notes and assets through the release-by-tag and release-by-id API endpoints, and download its attachments.

rootCause.explanation: The single-release API retrieves the record by ID/tag and serializes it without the write-access visibility restriction used by the web draft route.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Draft releases are hidden from users without write access on the web (the release page returns 404 and the draft isn't listed), but a read-only collaborator can fetch the draft's title, notes and assets through the release-by-tag and release-by-id API endpoints, and download its attachments.

sourceBugs.name: Draft releases and their assets are readable by read-only users through the API

reproductionPaths.expected: A user with only read permission gets 404 for a draft release on every endpoint, including the API and its attachment downloads, matching the web pages and release lists.
reproductionPaths.actual: As a read-only collaborator, the draft's web page returned 404 and the release lists omitted it, but GET /api/v1/repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases/tags/<tag>, /releases/<id> and /releases/<id>/assets returned the full draft (draft: true) with its assets, and the attachment downloaded.
reproSteps: As the owner, add a collaborator with Read permission.
As the owner, create a release with an attachment and save it as a draft.
As the read-only collaborator, open the draft's release page and confirm it returns 404.
As the same user, request the release by tag and by id through the API, then download its attachment.

logicalBugs.explanation: Opening a Releases (or Tags) list page number beyond the last page, for example going back to page 2 after its only release was deleted, shows the release count but no releases and no pagination controls, so there's no way from the list to reach the pages that do have releases. Gitea queries the requested page without moving it to the last page, and hides the pager when only one page exists.

rootCause.explanation: Release list queries use the requested offset without clamping to the final valid page, and the shared pager is hidden for one-page collections.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Opening a Releases (or Tags) list page number beyond the last page, for example going back to page 2 after its only release was deleted, shows the release count but no releases and no pagination controls, so there's no way from the list to reach the pages that do have releases. Gitea queries the requested page without moving it to the last page, and hides the pager when only one page exists.

sourceBugs.name: A releases page past the last page shows an empty list with no pagination

reproductionPaths.expected: A releases page past the end shows the last page that has releases, or at least keeps pagination so the earlier pages can be reached.
reproductionPaths.actual: After the only release on page 2 of 11 was deleted, going back to ?page=2 and refreshing showed "10 Releases" with no release entries and no pagination controls.
reproSteps: Create 11 releases so the Releases list has two pages, and open page 2.
Delete the only release on page 2.
Go back to the page 2 URL (for example with the browser's Back button) and refresh.
Check whether any releases or pagination controls are shown.
